items.note: Opened (Stadt Köln press release dated Wed 29 Jan 2020; heading 'Stadt Köln setzt die neue Parkgebührenordnung um', page title 'Parkscheinautomaten werden umgestellt'). All numbers match: about 2,750 machines, 1 euro per started 15 min in Innenstadt/Deutz, 0.50 euro in the other districts (previously per 20 min), 12,700 long-term spaces from 4 to 5 euros per 24 h, first increase after seven years, 1.8 million euros extra earmarked for KVB, council decision 26 Sep 2019. Only wrong point is tense: the release (29 Jan) says the conversion BEGINS on Monday 3 Feb 2020 and runs until about early May 2020; it does not say it had begun.
items.corrected_text: On 29 January 2020 the city announced that from 3 February 2020 it would start converting its roughly 2,750 parking meters, area by area and beginning in the centre, to the fee ordinance approved by the council on 26 September 2019: 1 euro per started 15 minutes in the centre and Deutz and 0.50 euro in the other districts (previously charged per 20 minutes), and long-term areas (12,700 spaces citywide) rising from 4 to 5 euros per 24 hours. It was the first increase after seven years of constant fees, with about 1.8 million euros of extra revenue earmarked for the KVB.

items.note: Opened (Stadt Köln release Wed 1 Jun 2022, 'Zwölfmonatiger Verkehrsversuch startet'). Matches: 12-month trial, pedestrian zone with 'Radfahrer frei', delivery traffic weekdays 6-11, decided end of 2021 by Bezirksvertretung Innenstadt, one section (Neuhöfferstraße to Graf-Geßler-Straße) excluded and gains quality through conversion of parking spaces, no number of spaces given. Only issue: the release says the zone WILL be set up on Friday 10 June 2022 (announcement), not that it started; and the page text says 'weiten Teilen der Straße' (large parts), consistent with 'most'.
items.corrected_text: On 1 June 2022 the city announced that on 10 June 2022 it would set up a pedestrian zone ('Radfahrer frei') on large parts of the Deutzer Freiheit for a twelve-month trial, as decided at the end of 2021 by the Bezirksvertretung Innenstadt; delivery traffic would be allowed on weekdays from 6 to 11 a.m. In the section between Neuhöfferstraße and Graf-Geßler-Straße, which had to be excluded from the trial, parking spaces are converted to other use; the release gives no number of spaces.

items.note: Opened (Stadt Köln release Mon 14 Nov 2022). Parkleitsystem garages 'mehr als 20.000 Stellplätze' Gesamtkapazität; ten P+R sites listed in the table with Weiden West 685, Marsdorf Haus Vorst 621, RheinEnergieStadion 571; P+R in Köln free up to 24 hours with a valid OEPNV ticket. All as written.

Opened (Stadt Köln release Tue 13 Dec 2022, heading 'Stadt und SWK schließen Betreibervertrag ... 1.000 weiterer E-Ladepunkte'). Contract for site selection, planning, building and operation of 1,000 further charging points in public street space, 30.6 million euros, completion of the 1,000th point 'vorgesehen' for 2026, the 2021 council decision wanted end of 2024 which proved unrealistic. All as written, and worded as a plan. Note: this is a 2022 plan; the page says nothing on progress, so the summary must not imply the 2026 target is on track.

Opened (IHK Köln page 'Verkehrsprojekt Trankgasse'; page is UNDATED, so the item date should be the retrieval month 2026-10; the 2023-03 given in the draft is the date of the IHK position paper, not of the page). The page is an advocacy page of the chamber of commerce, not a city source. Matches: spring 2023 package of temporary changes, car-free area between Marzellenstraße and am Domhof, Marzellen- and Komödienstraße made one-way, bicycle street between Tunisstraße and am Domhof, IHK plenary adopted a position paper in March 2023. Not as written: the garage exit is described as only 'theoretisch' guaranteed by a release for motor vehicles in a section of the bicycle streets (not plainly 'retained'); the page says IHK and many firms assess the redesign critically and that the routing must be evaluated thoroughly with the commercial neighbours, it does not itself summarise the position paper's content. Relevance to parking is marginal.
items.corrected_text: An undated page of the IHK Köln says that in spring 2023 a package of temporary changes to traffic routing around the Dom was implemented on Trankgasse: a car-free area between Marzellenstraße and am Domhof, Marzellen- and Komödienstraße converted to one-way streets and a bicycle street between Tunisstraße and am Domhof. Access from the Rheinuferstraße side to a hotel and the exit from the Tiefgarage am Dom towards Rheinuferstraße are, according to the page, 'theoretically' still possible through a release for motor traffic in a section of the bicycle streets. The IHK and many of its member firms assess the redesign critically, and its plenary adopted a position paper in March 2023 calling for the routing to be thoroughly evaluated with the local businesses.

items.note: Opened (parking.net, Mon 22 May 2023, republished Q-Park press release, no AI label). 896 spaces over 6 levels, 24 charging stations, 'Book and Reserve' service 'will also be equipped', future cashless and ticketless parking technology; announcement of a new management contract. All as written and correctly worded as announced/planned. Only the stored title differs from the page headline. Source is the operator's own press release (promotional).
items.corrected_title: Q-Park Operations Germany GmbH & Co. KG Takes Over the I/D Cologne Car Park in Cologne-Mülheim

items.note: Opened (Stadt Köln release Fri 17 Nov 2023). Adapted proposal sent to the committees: 100/110/120 euros by vehicle length (to 4,109 mm; 4,110-4,709 mm; 4,710-5,600 mm), May 2023 proposal of 330-390 euros withdrawn after the Federal Administrative Court's Freiburg ruling, 47 residents' parking zones with about 51,400 spaces, 61,020 permits at 31 Dec 2022, about 20 percent fewer permits assumed and about 5.3 million euros a year. Correctly worded as a proposal.

Opened (Stadt Köln release Tue 19 Dec 2023). About 722 coaches registered over the last three weekends, about 85 percent from abroad, P22 with KVB shuttle to Heumarkt; Lanxess-Arena and Kaiser-Wilhelm-Ring garages well used; late-afternoon queues in front of full garages (the page does not name which garages were full). Matches as written.

Opened (parking.net, Wed 17 Apr 2024, republished Q-Park press release, no AI label). From 1 May 2024, Vogelsanger Straße 84, 1,043 spaces on two levels, around 569 for long-term parkers, 2.00 euros per hour and 29.00 euros daily maximum, licence-plate recognition and publicly usable EV charging spaces planned. All as written. The tariff is the operator's announced rate for May 2024, not verified as current. Stored title differs from the page headline.
items.corrected_title: Q-Park Is Expanding Its Portfolio In Cologne

items.note: Opened (Stadt Köln release Fri 27 Sep 2024). Fee 30 to 100 euros from 1 Oct 2024 with transitional rule until 28 Feb 2025; from 1 Mar 2025 tiered 100/110/120 by length (up to 4,109 mm 100; above 4,709 mm 120; between 110); owners of vehicles over 5,600 mm no longer entitled. All as written, and the item is dated and attributed to the city statement of Sep 2024. Caveat for the summary: the page only shows what the city announced in Sept 2024; this check did not find a 2026 source confirming the tiers are still in force, so say 'according to the city's September 2024 statement'.

Opened (Stadt Köln release Fri 22 Nov 2024). Draft Parkgebührenordnung 2025 ('Beschlussvorlage', politics deliberating): keep two zones, short-term 5 euros/h (from 4) in Innenstadt/Deutz, 2.50 euros (from 2) in districts 2-9, long-term 30 euros/day, seven-day ticket dropped, long-term parking inside the Kölner Ringe ended, about 50,000 managed spaces, 21.25 million euros fee income in 2023, council decision planned February 2025. Properly worded as a proposal.

Opened (t-online Köln, Sebastian Hahn, 28.05.2025; not labelled AI). Matches: on Tuesday 27 May the council again postponed the decision on the new Parkgebührenordnung after CDU Fraktionsgeschäftsführer Niklas Kienitz requested further deliberation (as at the early-April session); proposal 5 euros/h centre (from 4), 2.50 euros elsewhere (from 2), 24-hour car parks 30 euros/day (from at most 5). Not as written: the page says only that, according to party circles, further delays 'angesichts der im Herbst anstehenden Kommunalwahl nicht unwahrscheinlich' are likely; it does not say 'September 2025' or that a decision before the election was 'unlikely', and it is t-online's own attribution to party circles, not press reports in general. Medium-quality news source.
items.corrected_text: On 27 May 2025 the council again postponed its decision on the proposed new Parkgebührenordnung (5 euros per hour in the centre instead of 4, 2.50 euros in the other districts instead of 2, 30 euros a day instead of at most 5 on the city's 24-hour car parks) after the CDU group asked for more time to deliberate, as it had at the early-April session. t-online, citing party circles, reported that further delays were not unlikely given the municipal election due in the autumn.

items.note: Opened (Stadt Köln release Mon 11 Aug 2025, 'Autos und Fahrräder unter einem Dach'). Administration has put a Beschlussvorlage into the committee process for a combined car and bicycle Parkpalette at Weiden-West; estimated cost 21.25 million euros; own share of city and KVB falls from 10.13 to 2.9 million euros through higher grants; 66 planned car spaces become about 130 bicycle boxes and more than 200 bicycle stands; award (Vergabe) to a general contractor for further planning and construction on 4 July 2025; supplementary bicycle order needs a political decision. Correctly worded as a plan/proposal. Note: topic 'ev' is wrong, this is P+R / bicycle parking (not EV charging); the stored title is the page's heading.

Opened (Stadt Köln release Mon 15 Sep 2025). Closed to the public 'ab sofort bis auf Weiteres' for investigations of the structure, about 50 concrete columns to be sampled, reopening date unknown, alternatives Am Dom, Philharmonie, An Farina, Hauptbahnhof, Heumarkt (entrance Große Neugasse). Nuance: spaces still usable during the investigation are reserved for long-term parkers and residents. The koeln.de garage page on 21 Oct 2026 still says the garage remains closed 'bis auf Weiteres', so the closure appears ongoing.

Opened (Stadt Köln release Fri 14 Nov 2025, announcement of the Advent 2025 plan). Matches: connected garages have a capacity of 22,000 spaces; 27 LED variable-message boards on the main access roads show occupancy of the parking quarters; parking tickets at Lanxess-Arena P1, P2, P4 and Kaiser-Wilhelm-Ring become a group day ticket for up to five people on the four Advent Saturdays (also Haus Vorst, where a ticket is handed out). Not as written: the Heumarkt statement. The page says the approach from the Deutzer Brücke ramp via Markmannsgasse to the old-town Rheinufer and to the Parkhaus Heumarkt is closed 10 a.m.-10 p.m. from 27 Nov to 23 Dec 2025 and reserved for emergency vehicles, buses and taxis; the garage itself is not said to be closed. It is an announcement of measures, so wording must be future/planned.
items.corrected_text: For Advent 2025 the city announced that the garages connected to its Parkleitsystem have a capacity of 22,000 spaces and that 27 LED variable-message boards on the main access roads show the occupancy of the parking quarters. On the four Advent Saturdays (29 November, 6, 13 and 20 December 2025) the parking tickets of the Lanxess-Arena garages P1, P2 and P4 and of the Tiefgarage Kaiser-Wilhelm-Ring would serve as group day tickets for up to five people on buses and trains. From 27 November to 23 December 2025, between 10 a.m. and 10 p.m., the approach from the Deutzer Brücke via Markmannsgasse to the Rheinufer and the Parkhaus Heumarkt was to be closed, reserved for emergency vehicles, buses and taxis.

items.note: Opened (Stadt Köln release Wed 17 Dec 2025). Matches: council decided on Tue 16 Dec 2025 to adjust fees to an average hourly rate of 2.10 euros (previously 1.44 on average); example Breslauer Platz 0.60 to 0.80 euro per started 20 min, daily maximum 18 to 24 euros; new fees 'zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt', 'nach aktuellem Planungsstand voraussichtlich zum 1. Februar 2026'. Not as written: the city says it OWNS eight (Am Dom, Breslauer Platz/Hbf, Philharmonie, Kaiser-Wilhelm-Ring, Neptunplatz, Kalk, Mülheim, Parkhaus Am Zoo) and is only PART-owner of Tiefgarage Groß St. Martin, so 'nine city-owned garages' is inaccurate; the page also lists nine facilities but says Am Dom stays at 0.80/24 euros, so not every garage rises. The start date stays a plan on this page and is NOT confirmed by any city source I opened. (Side observation, not confirmation: koeln.de garage pages for Philharmonie and Groß St. Martin show 0.80 euro per 20 min / 24 euros with base data of 4 Feb 2026, consistent with but not proof of the new rates being applied; these are an aggregator listing.)
items.corrected_text: On 16 December 2025 the council decided to raise parking fees in the city's garages (Tiefgaragen Am Dom, Breslauer Platz/Hauptbahnhof, Groß St. Martin, Philharmonie, Kaiser-Wilhelm-Ring, Mülheim, Kalk, Neptunplatz and Parkhaus Am Zoo; the city owns all but Groß St. Martin, of which it is part-owner) to an average hourly rate of 2.10 euros, up from 1.44 euros. For example, Breslauer Platz rises from 0.60 to 0.80 euro per started 20 minutes with the daily maximum going from 18 to 24 euros, while Tiefgarage Am Dom stays at 0.80 euro and 24 euros. According to the city's planning at the time, the new rates were expected to start on 1 February 2026; the page does not confirm that they did.

items.note: Opened (t-online Köln, 09.09.2026, byline 't-online, shh'; not labelled AI-written). Matches: headline/standfirst say an increase remains open and 'Einen Ratsbeschluss dazu gibt es nicht'; proposal 5 euros/h in the centre (from 4), 2.50 euros elsewhere (from 2), 24-hour car parks 30 euros/day ('25 Euro mehr als bislang'); the topic has not been on the council agenda since the local election. Not as written: the city spokeswoman said only that the administration submitted the draft to the Verkehrsausschuss (now Mobilitätsausschuss) on 26 Nov 2024 and that since 13 Feb 2025 the draft 'liegt dem Rat ... zur Beschlussfassung vor und wird dort beraten'. 'Without a vote' and 'not on the agenda since the election' are t-online's own statements, not the spokeswoman's. The article also says the draft 2027/28 budget announces fee adjustments including for garages while short-term street parking stays untouched for now, and that the political majority is lacking. Single news source.
items.corrected_text: t-online Köln reported on 9 September 2026 that there is still no council decision on the proposed Parkgebührenordnung (5 euros per hour in the centre instead of 4, 2.50 euros in the other districts instead of 2, 30 euros a day instead of 5 on 24-hour car parks). A city spokeswoman told the paper that the administration submitted the draft to the mobility committee on 26 November 2024 and that it has been before the council for a decision since 13 February 2025. According to t-online itself, the topic has not been on the council agenda since the municipal election, and short-term street parking stays unchanged for now because the political majority is lacking.

items.note: Opened (koeln.de overview page, 'Stand 21.10.2026 08:53', data source stated as Stadt Köln via Mobilithek). The free-space counts are rendered as images; read from the page markup, the overview showed 38 free at Groß St. Martin (as drafted), 914 at Lanxess-Arena P1 and 1,345 at Köln Arcaden, not the 932 and 1,365 in the draft (live figures change minute to minute and the draft snapshot cannot be reproduced). The Groß St. Martin detail page (Stand 21.10.2026 08:52) shows 38 free, 213 spaces in total (185 short-term), 80 Cent per started 20 min / 24 euros, 'Parkhaus-Basisdaten 04.02.2026', and its own text says the garage 'bleibt bis auf Weiteres für die Öffentlichkeit geschlossen'. So the conflict with the closure notice is real. Page is a live, undated-by-design data page: retrieval date 2026-10-21 is correct. Low-value, single snapshot, aggregator (koeln.de) rather than the city.
items.corrected_text: The koeln.de live overview of city garages (data from the Stadt Köln Parkleitsystem via the Mobilithek) showed on 21 October 2026 at about 8:53 a.m., for example, 1,345 free spaces at Köln Arcaden, 914 at Lanxess-Arena P1 and 38 shown free at Groß St. Martin. The Groß St. Martin detail page lists 213 spaces in total, 185 of them for short-term parkers, and a tariff of 80 cents per started 20 minutes and 24 euros per day, but also says the garage remains closed to the public until further notice, so the 38 free spaces conflict with the closure notice. This is a single morning snapshot of live data, not a utilisation statistic.

corrected_summary: Köln manages about 50,000 paid on-street spaces in two fee zones (Innenstadt/Deutz and districts 2 to 9). The current street tariff dates from a fee ordinance approved by the council on 26 September 2019 and implemented from February 2020 (1 euro per started 15 minutes in the centre and Deutz, 0.50 euro elsewhere, long-term areas 5 euros per 24 hours). In November 2024 the administration proposed raising short-term parking to 5 euros an hour in the centre and 2.50 euros elsewhere and long-term parking to 30 euros a day; the council postponed the decision on 27 May 2025, and t-online reported on 9 September 2026 that there is still no council decision, with the draft before the council since 13 February 2025. For residents' parking, the city announced in September 2024 that the annual permit fee rose from 30 to 100 euros on 1 October 2024 and would be tiered at 100, 110 and 120 euros by vehicle length from 1 March 2025; a 2026 confirmation of this was not checked. On 16 December 2025 the council decided to raise tariffs in nine city garages (average hourly rate from 1.44 to 2.10 euros), with the city expecting a start around 1 February 2026, which was not confirmed from a city source. The Tiefgarage Groß St. Martin was closed to the public on 15 September 2025 for structural investigations, and the koeln.de garage page still said on 21 October 2026 that it remains closed until further notice. For Advent 2025 the city said its Parkleitsystem covers garages with 22,000 spaces and 27 LED boards; occupancy data is also published through the Mobilithek. Q-Park announced management contracts for the I/D Cologne garage in Mülheim (May 2023, 896 spaces) and the Barthonia Forum in Ehrenfeld (from 1 May 2024, 1,043 spaces). Access policy is changing at the edges: a twelve-month Deutzer Freiheit pedestrian-zone trial was announced for June 2022 and temporary traffic changes at Trankgasse near the Dom were made in spring 2023 (criticised by the IHK). Stadtwerke Köln signed a contract in December 2022 for 1,000 further public charging points with the last one planned for 2026 (progress not checked), and in August 2025 the city proposed a combined car and bicycle Parkpalette at the Weiden-West P+R. The sources found do not show current Umweltzone rules, Mobilstation figures or a Köln-wide utilisation statistic.
